messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] All atlas in braingraph has even numbers of the areas, and it's effect on the custom atlas.
messages.subject_clean: [brainGraph-help] All atlas in braingraph has even numbers of the areas, and it's effect on the custom atlas.
messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the reply.
I confirmed that it's 'B'.  based on the code.
https://github.com/cwatson/brainGraph/blob/a0d13aea831fbb708c9fb984816e9edda616bbdd/R/import.R#L137
However, Still braingraph can't get the areas maked as 'B'.
For example, when I (wrongly) change the 'B', to 'R', everything works properly, but 'B' hemisphere with Cerebellum nor Brainstem doesn't work.
While reading the code lines, I guess you might allowed 'B' in very limited usecase (like specific atlas).
Would you kindly check this, please?

Bests,
J.

On Thursday, January 18, 2024 at 1:57:27 AM UTC+9 Chris Watson wrote:
> I think you can set some of them to "B" which means "bilateral" (if I remember correctly; I wrote it a long time ago). So try that.
>
> On Wed, Jan 17, 2024 at 9:16 AM J <june...@empathy-research.org> wrote:
> > Dear Chris,
> >
> > I found all the atlas in github has even numbers of the areas.
> > For several weeks, I struggled with the custom atlas, and found this interesting common ground.
> >
> > Whenever I try to use the custom atlas with different numbers of areas per hemisphere, or three levels of lobes L, R, and M for brainstem or other 'middle' areas, I get
> > task 1 failed - "invalid 'length.out' value".
> >
> > Does the hemisphere and lobes are mandatory for running make_brainGraphList?
> > Is it impossible to use the function with some 'middle' areas?
> >
> > Bests,
> > J.

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] All atlas in braingraph has even numbers of the areas, and it's effect on the custom atlas.

messages.body_plain:
I found the solution after several trial-and-error experiemnts : )  the 'B' is used at certain stage, bot the correct one is 'both'. When I put the 'both' for 'hemi' column, the issue resolved.
Sincerely appreciate to your awesome tool, and contribution to open science.
